filename: Understanding Ice Crystal Habit Diversity with Self-Supervised Learning.pdf
title: Understanding Ice Crystal Habit Diversity with Self-Supervised Learning
venue: Tackling Climate Change with Machine Learning: workshop at NeurIPS 2025
code_availability: Public third-party code repositories referenced in footnotes: iBOT (https://github.com/bytedance/ibot/) and SSL data curation (https://github.com/facebookresearch/ssl-data-curation). Code for this study is not explicitly provided in the manuscript.
testbed_rationale: The datasets consist of microscopic in situ cloud particle images and co-located flight measurements for self-supervised representation learning and habit classification, rather than grid-cell forcing/target states suitable for atmospheric parameterization or emulation.
pain_points: Class imbalance in self-supervised learning datasets leading to prototype collapse or poor representation balance in DINO models.
Very high computational cost of self-supervised learning pre-training on millions of domain-specific scientific images.
Difficulty of scaling manual habit labeling for millions of in situ cloud particle probe images.
extraction_notes: The paper uses self-supervised learning (iBOT-vMF with ViT-Small) to learn latent representations of ice crystal morphology without manual supervision, and validates it using a hand-labeled test set and a downstream application relating concentration parameter kappa to temperature, particle size, and campaign.
